Class GTNetGrantService

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetGrantService
@Service public class GTNetGrantService extends Object
Answers whether a peer may be served a kind of data exchange.

The documented state machine goes Connected → DataExchangeActive on an accepted data request, with a revoke as the way back, but nothing enforced it: every inbound data handler tested only this instance's own accept flag, which is a global "do I serve this kind at all" rather than a decision about one peer. Possession of a token plus a globally open entity was therefore sufficient, and a peer that had merely completed a handshake could ask for everything.

The grant is the GTNetConfigEntity hanging off the peer's GTNetEntity for that kind. It is written when a data request is accepted in either direction, and a revoke sets its exchange flag to false. It is local: syncGtNetEntitiesFromDTO deliberately leaves it alone when a peer's published state is synchronized, so a peer cannot grant itself anything by what it publishes about itself.

The grant carries no direction. The same row is created whether we requested and they accepted, or they requested and we accepted, so a grant in either direction authorises serving. Giving it a direction is a schema change and is deliberately not part of this work.

    • hasAnyGrant

      public boolean hasAnyGrant(GTNet remoteGTNet)
      Whether this peer has a grant for at least one syncable kind.

      This is the form the exchange-sync code needs. One sync request covers every kind at once, so refusing it wholesale because a peer holds only one of two grants would end an exchange that both sides agreed to.

      Parameters:
      remoteGTNet - the peer asking, null when the peer is unknown
      Returns:
      true when at least one syncable kind is granted

      the grant row, empty when the peer never had one for that kind

    • clearGrant

      public boolean clearGrant(GTNet remoteGTNet, IExchangeKindType kind)
      Ends a grant without creating one.

      This is what a rejection and a revoke leave behind, and it is deliberately the only state either of them writes. Setting acceptRequest and serverState on the peer's row instead would look like a state change and be undone by the peer's very next envelope, because those two fields are re-synchronized from what the peer publishes about itself.

      Parameters:
      remoteGTNet - the peer whose grant ends
      kind - the exchange kind that is no longer granted
      Returns:
      true when a grant was present and has been cleared
